title: Authoritative versus advisory deterministic evidence for graph generation
question: Does deterministic evidence improve final graph construction when it is advisory rather than authoritative?
hypothesis: Raw text plus a non-authoritative evidence packet will produce more complete valid graphs than raw text or an enforced Stage-1 skeleton.

change_under_test.description: Compare raw text, evidence-before-generation, authoritative skeleton, and raw-draft-then-evidence-review.

control.description: Raw-text graph generation on four cross-clause and conditional cases.

experimental.description: Raw draft followed by evidence review

intentionally_not_compared: causal effect independent of stochastic Stage-1 variation
interpretation: Advisory evidence did not outperform raw text. Authoritative Stage 1 performed worst. Evidence modes exposed substantial loss between high Stage-1 node recall and final graph materialization.

do_not_prioritize: full evidence-packet dumps as the default graph-generation prompt
decision.next_test: Use a narrowly targeted evidence delta on a frozen raw draft.

limitations: Stage-1 extraction and graph drafts were not frozen across arms.
Final graph metrics for early arms were rescored from printed admitted graphs after the runs.
Temperature zero does not guarantee bitwise-identical OpenAI outputs.
